scope.primary_endpoint: Full fixed pre-request serial token received by the common event-driven socket reader
scope.primary_interval: Immediately before QEMU spawn through reader timestamp; includes startup, QMP setup and stock Linux boot
scope.token_guest_position: After CPU pin, iopl, registration and setup; immediately before flight.ready request
scope.execution_contract_limit: TCG without icount, ordinary 1 ns/instruction icount, and Sim 50 ps/instruction use distinct clock contracts; latency ratios are not equal-instruction overhead ratios
scope.native_stop: Only Sim is authenticated and stopped at request raw+1/logical+50; this secondary endpoint is later than the shared serial milestone
scope.stock_icount: Post-marker QMP stopped replay count includes stop latency and is not the exact token instruction coordinate
scope.cpu_accounting: Stock counters are sampled shortly after marker delivery; Sim counters after native pause acknowledgement. Neither is an exact marker CPU coordinate
scope.device_projection_manifest: Schema validation only; no claim to capture complete modeled device-state values
scope.guest_change: The added serial marker creates a new initramfs and new Sim witness. Old guest coordinates are not compared to this guest
scope.failure_policy: Every start retained, no retries or replacements. Only recognized natural boot/readiness failures may continue; invalid witnesses and infrastructure errors abort
scope.percentages: Separate microbenchmark gains are not added to Linux boot percentages

raw_results.scope:
Compare ordinary TCG and Sim through the same complete serial milestone.

All rows boot identical stock kernel and initramfs bytes. The primary interval
starts before QEMU spawn and ends when the common socket reader receives the
complete pre-request token. It includes emulator startup, QMP setup and boot;
protocol allocation and post-marker diagnostics are outside the interval.

Ordinary TCG without icount, ordinary TCG with 1 ns per instruction, and Sim
with 50 ps per instruction use different execution contracts. Their same-workload
boot latency comparison is not a measurement of equal-instruction overhead.
Sim's authenticated native stop, full RAM, registers and timer witness are
qualified separately after the common marker. Stock post-marker QMP stops are
not exact token coordinates. CPU accounting endpoints are recorded per row.

Build the new guest and driver with the AOS phase2.tcgLinuxSerialGuest and
phase2.tcgLinuxSerialPerformanceDriver targets using local builders. Pass each
row explicitly as --row LABEL MODE QEMU_BINARY PLUGIN_OR_DASH. Modes are tcg,
tcg-icount and sim; ordinary TCG takes '-' for the plugin. No plugins are loaded
in ordinary TCG rows, even when the emulator supports them. Repeated rounds
rotate row positions and then reverse the rotations. Every start, exit, stream,
raw result and failed attempt is retained; no failed trial is retried or replaced.

plugin_three_pairs.measurement_scope: Three quiet alternating pairs, six scheduled starts. Same x786 QEMU; only real plugin implementation changes

raw_results.scope:
Compare ordinary TCG and Sim through the same complete serial milestone.

All rows boot identical stock kernel and initramfs bytes. The primary interval
starts before QEMU spawn and ends when the common socket reader receives the
complete pre-request token. It includes emulator startup, QMP setup and boot;
protocol allocation and post-marker diagnostics are outside the interval.

Ordinary TCG without icount, ordinary TCG with 1 ns per instruction, and Sim
with 50 ps per instruction use different execution contracts. Their same-workload
boot latency comparison is not a measurement of equal-instruction overhead.
Sim's authenticated native stop, full RAM, registers and timer witness are
qualified separately after the common marker. Stock post-marker QMP stops are
not exact token coordinates. CPU accounting endpoints are recorded per row.

Build the new guest and driver with the AOS phase2.tcgLinuxSerialGuest and
phase2.tcgLinuxSerialPerformanceDriver targets using local builders. Pass each
row explicitly as --row LABEL MODE QEMU_BINARY PLUGIN_OR_DASH. Modes are tcg,
tcg-icount and sim; ordinary TCG takes '-' for the plugin. No plugins are loaded
in ordinary TCG rows, even when the emulator supports them. Repeated rounds
rotate row positions and then reverse the rotations. Every start, exit, stream,
raw result and failed attempt is retained; no failed trial is retried or replaced.
